leads.title: Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810 - decriminalisation of sodomy
leads.documents: Decriminalisation of private same-sex relations in France and by extension French colonies adopting the Code; basis for legal status in New Caledonia as French territory.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private, retained in Penal Code of 1810 and followed in nations and French colonies that adopted the Code

leads.title: Law of 1999 creating PACS (pacte civil de solidarite) - Jospin Government
leads.documents: Registered domestic partnership for same-sex and unmarried opposite-sex couples with most legal protections of marriage; applicable framework preceding marriage equality.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as enacted in 1999 for both same-sex and unmarried opposite-sex couples

leads.title: Law No. 2013-404 opening marriage to same-sex couples - Journal Officiel
leads.documents: Legalises same-sex marriage and joint adoption in all of France including all overseas departments and territories including New Caledonia; documents marriage equality enforcement.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as National Assembly vote 329-229 on 12 Feb 2013 and 23 April 2013, Constitutional Council ruling 17 May 2013 that law is constitutional, signed 18 May 2013 by President Francois Hollande, published next day in Journal Officiel; overseas section states same-sex marriage is legal in all overseas departments and territories and 2 deputies from New Caledonia voted in favor

leads.title: B. vs France - European Court of Human Rights 1992
leads.documents: Court ruling that ended French legislature ban on legal gender change for transgender people even after medical/surgical transition.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as 1992 case, B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed this

leads.title: Discrimination protections - Law of 1985, Law of July 2012, Law of 18 November 2016 amending Penal Code article 225-1
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination on sexual orientation (1985) and sexual identity/gender identity (2012, wording replaced with gender identity in 2016); core rights machinery for LGBTQ protection.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as national legislation enacted 1985, French Parliament added sexual identity in July 2012, new law 18 November 2016 amended article 225-1 to replace sexual identity with gender identity; ILGA-Europe criticism noted

leads.title: Code du travail (Labour Code) Chapter 2 anti-discrimination provision
leads.documents: Employment/recruitment/internship protection explicitly listing sexual orientation and gender identity alongside other grounds.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; quoted in article as: No person may be excluded from a recruitment process... on account of origin, gender, morals, sexual orientation, gender identity...

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 and Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 Title 3 articles 20 and 21 - Haute autorite
leads.documents: Hate-crime/speech machinery: makes homophobic/sexist/racist comments illegal, increases penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation, creates Haute autorite de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'egalite.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as National Assembly approved amendment 31 Dec 2004, max penalty 45,000 euro fine and/or 12 months imprisonment, first conviction of MP Christian Vanneste Jan 2006 later cancelled by Court of Cassation

leads.title: Law No. 2016-1547 of 18 November 2016 - legal gender change without surgery/sterilisation
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to legally change gender without sex reassignment surgery, forced sterilisation, psychiatrist certificates; requires court application; registry office for first name; effective 1 Jan 2017.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as Senate approved 6 Nov 2015, National Assembly 24 May 2016, joint session 12 July 2016, Senate 28 Sept, Assembly 12 Oct, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov 2016, published Journal Officiel next day, took effect 1 Jan 2017; MP Pascale Crozon introduced bill

leads.title: 2017 aggravating-circumstance provision and 2022 Court of Appeal parentage ruling
leads.documents: Transphobia as aggravating cause for all crimes punishable by prison (2017); transgender woman recognised as mother of child conceived before transition (2022 appeal).
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as In 2017, transphobia became a cause of aggravation for all crimes that can be punished by prison; In 2022, a court of appeal ruled that a transgender woman should be considered the mother

leads.title: Law banning conversion therapy - published 1 February 2022
leads.documents: Criminal ban on conversion therapy; documents state enforcement tool relevant to visitor safety.
leads.detail: No URL in article text; cited as passed Senate 7 Dec 2020, concurred by National Assembly 25 Jan 2022, officially published 1 Feb 2022; proposal punishments 2 years imprisonment and/or 30,000 euro fine, MP Laurence Vanceunebrock-Mialon proposal
